model.name: Pratibimb fusion model
model.task: Binary: cardiovascular strain episode onset within 72 h, scored once per night from the latest synced data
model.algorithm: LightGBM gradient-boosted trees on dynamic (wearable) features, twin-adjusted residuals and a compact static tower of eight record features; patient-level 5-fold CV repeated on three patient splits; Platt calibration on pooled out-of-fold scores; the five fold models form the bag for the probability band; NightSignal-style rule run alongside

data.split: patient-level 5-fold cross-validation repeated on three patient splits (seeds 42, 43, 44); every metric on pooled out-of-fold predictions; headline numbers are the mean of the three splits
sources: Synthetic wearable streams with labelled strain episodes and unlabelled infection, lifestyle and missing-data confounders (twin.data.wearables)

model.ablation_note: At a matched 90% event sensitivity on out-of-fold predictions: watch-only (HR, HRV, sleep, steps, SpO2, respiratory rate) alerted inside 233 of 242 infection-like windows at 0.194 false alerts per patient-day; adding the home BP cuff gave 164 windows at 0.1169; the fused model with the record gave 173 windows at 0.126. The blood-pressure cuff is what separates strain from a cold. Mean over three patient splits: AUROC 0.578 for the record alone, 0.804 for the watch alone, 0.87 for watch + cuff and 0.876 fused (fused ahead of watch + cuff on 2 of 3 splits).
model.twin_note: Twin adjustment: the personal physiology engine removes the part of each night's heart rate, HRV and BP change that the person's own sleep and activity explain, and the record tells the model how to read the heart-rate rise (beta blockers dampen it). Mean over three patient splits: without it the fused model reaches AUROC 0.851 and catches 64% of events at the false-alert budget; with it, AUROC 0.876 and 70% (better AUROC on 3 of 3 splits).
model.ceiling_note: Even an oracle static prior (the generator's own risk multiplier) adds only a little over the wearable-only model: on a 72-hour horizon, when matters more than who. The EHR stream's job is prioritisation, interpretation (diabetic silent episodes, beta-blocker dampening) and the static risk panel, not timing.

operating_points.score_mapping: 0 to 0, p_watch to 30, p_urgent to 60, 1 to 100 (piecewise linear on calibrated probability)

physiology.note: On the synthetic cohort the generator's true per-person slopes are known, so the twin's recovery of each person's physiology is measured directly. Pooled = the twin's estimate; raw = per-person regression with no pooling; population = one slope for everyone.

calibration.method: Platt scaling (logistic on logit of raw score) fit on pooled out-of-fold predictions

limitations: Trained and evaluated on a synthetic cohort. Reported numbers describe how well the twin recovers injected episodes, not clinical performance.
Strain-episode ground truth is defined by the generator; real adverse events are heterogeneous and rarer.
Consumer-watch data syncs hourly to daily; the twin scores once per night and cannot see minute-level emergencies.
Framingham 2008 under-estimates risk in South Asians; the WHO 2019 SEAR chart is the planned replacement.
No validation on any Indian clinical dataset yet; BODH benchmarking and an ABDM-sandbox pilot are roadmap items.

Personal response slopes come from everyday swings in sleep and activity (observational, not randomised); medicine, salt and alcohol effects in the what-if are population estimates because the twin has no personal data on them.
Not a medical device. Outputs are decision support for a registered practitioner, never a diagnosis.
